search.note: Careers Site API for ONE company (config company_subdomain): GET https://{company}.recruitee.com/api/offers/ 'Returns a collection of published company jobs'. Its only filters are department and tag names, so query/location/page/limit are not sent: every published offer comes back in one response — filter client-side and do not request further pages. id is the offer slug (apply takes it); requirements, highlight, remote/on_site/hybrid, locations[], employment_type_code, salary {min, max, period, currency} (amounts are strings), options_cv/options_phone/options_cover_letter and open_questions are in raw.

apply.note: Submits a REAL application to the employer in the configured candidate's name (applicant_name/applicant_email/applicant_phone config): POST /api/offers/{offer_slug}/candidates with JSON {candidate: {name, email, phone, cover_letter, remote_cv_url}} — 'creating a candidate via this API is like a candidate applying for a job and it will trigger all actions connected with it (like sending an application confirmation email)'. id is the offer slug from search; resume_url must be a publicly downloadable CV link ('Link to file saved on some external website'). Name and email are always required; phone and CV are required unless the offer's form turns them off (see options_phone/options_cv on the offer). Screening-question answers (open_questions) cannot be sent by this tool, so offers with required questions will be refused.

not_offered.me: The Careers Site API has no account endpoint (its token covers only /offers, /offers/:id and /offers/:offer_slug/candidates).
not_offered.get_posting: The Careers Site API reference documents only the offers list and the apply endpoint; the documented /offers/:id is the ATS API (https://api.recruitee.com/c/{company_id}/offers/{id}) with a different token. Re-read the record from the search hit.
not_offered.list_messages: No candidate messaging in the Careers Site API.
